items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: I would try to pick a lot of those things that I think brought me along, that turned me on to the music. Clifford Brown and Max Roach.

ctx.x: If you had a little audience and you were trying to get them turned on to jazz, and you had an hour or something and you had a CD player, what kind of recordings would you pick from jazz history?

I would try to squeeze in as much real live recordings. Some Louis Armstrong, some Duke Ellington, Billie Holiday of course and then probably get to some Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers. Cannonball. I mean there would be so much I would try to pack in. And I would try to pick a lot of those things that I think brought me along, that turned me on to the music. Clifford Brown and Max Roach. But singers. Singers I think is always a good way of coming in.
[Phone ringing. Excuse me for a moment]

items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: Like sometimes like when Max would call me up... I had so much respect for him... they would call me up for gigs

ctx.x: Again, this is sometimes a hard question. What’s the best gig or series of gigs you ever had, and on the other hand what might have been the worst?

I don’t know if I can ever say I’ve had a worst. I mean all the gigs I’ve had have been important and great to me. Because I’m still a fan of the music. You know what I mean? Every time I can still get on the bandstand with those guys that I have posted on my wall, you know, I have the album covers tacked up or I had read the interviews or you know what I mean? For me to have them still be around and call me up. Wow. You know what I mean? Like sometimes like when Max would call me up. Like wow. I actually…
Nice. That’s a great sentiment. Playing with those guys that were on the wall.
